content.title: GOVERNMENT OF THE DISTRICT OF COLUMBIA
content.text:
GOVERNMENT OF THE DISTRICT OF COLUMBIA
 Department on Disability Services
 Developmental Disabilities Administration

 Silver Alert Information Sheet and Consent Form

The Department on Disability Services (DDS), Developmental Disabilities Administration (DDA)
has partnered with the Metropolitan Police Department (MPD) to implement Silver Alert for
District of Columbia (DC) residents served by DDA.

What is Silver Alert?

Silver Alert is similar to the AMBER Alert. It is a public notification system designed to
broadcast information about missing persons who are at high risk for injury or harm if
they are lost or missing; such as, seniors with dementia and an adult of any age who has
an Intellectual/Developmental Disability, in order to aid in their safe return home.

Silver Alert is overseen by the MPD effective October 24, 2013 per special order (SO-13-10); in
collaboration with the District of Columbia Office of Aging (DCOA), Homeland Security and
Emergency Management Agency (HSEMA), Maryland/DC/Delaware Broadcasters’ Association,
and District Department of Transportation (DDOT).

Why is Silver Alert important?

Silver Alert provides protection for people whose age or disability put them in imminent danger
or at grave risk of bodily harm, if they are lost or missing, by disseminating information about
the missing person by using road signs, reverse 911, social media, news broadcasts, and/or the
Emergency Alert System (EAS). Silver Alert helps in the locating missing persons in order to
safely return them home.

What if my loved one lives outside of DC?

DDA has an agreement with MPD that allows people who receive DDA services but live outside
of DC to access Silver Alert.

Do I have to participate in Silver Alert?

You do not have to participate in Silver Alert. Whether or not you enroll in Silver Alert does not
impact on the services you receive from DDA. If you or your loved one is lost or missing, DDA
will still follow the Missing Person Protocol however, a Silver Alert will not be issued on your
behalf. Each year at your ISP you will be asked if you would like to be exempt from Silver Alert.
If you do not wish to participate and change your mind, but it is not time for your annual ISP,
you may do so by notifying your Service Coordinator.
